poolNote: A hard cap, committed here before the window opened. 200,000,000 $115792 — twenty per cent of the one billion circulating after the one billion burn. The pool cannot grow and it cannot shrink. Every allocation below is a pro-rata slice of this fixed number, so no combination of participants can over-commit it.
rule: Allocation weight = (the MINIMUM balance you held, measured at the anchor slot, at every undisclosed checkpoint, and at the window close) x (your tenure multiplier). Your payout is your weight divided by the sum of all weights, multiplied by the pool. You are paid on the least you ever held, scaled by how early you were holding it.
base: Minimum balance across the anchor slot, all five checkpoints, and the window close. Sell at any point and your weight is permanently capped at that trough, including at checkpoints you have not seen yet.

finalMeasurement.note: The one measurement whose time is public. It is the window close, it was always published, and it counts toward your minimum exactly like a checkpoint does. Publishing it costs nothing, because a measurement everyone knows about cannot be dodged - you either hold to the close or you do not. It exists so there is no unmeasured stretch at the end of the window in which selling is free.
finalMeasurement.affectsTierNote: It counts toward your BASE, not your TIER. Tenure is still decided by the earliest checkpoint at which you held.

tiers.label: Original entropy
tiers.test: Held at or above the dust floor at the anchor slot — a block that had already passed before any of this was published.
tiers.note: Unfarmable by construction. You either were there or you were not.

tiers.label: Early
tiers.test: Not at the anchor, but holding by checkpoint one or two.
tiers.note: The checkpoint times are secret, so the only way to be certain of catching an early one is to be holding now.

tiers.label: Mid
tiers.test: First holding at checkpoint three or four.

tiers.label: Late
tiers.test: First holding at the final checkpoint only.
tiers.note: Still a real allocation. Late is not zero — it is just worth a third of what the people who were already here get.

bonus.label: Found the entropy
bonus.test: Located the hidden recovery screen on the site and submitted the address-bound code it issues.
bonus.note: Added to the multiplier rather than multiplied by it, which means it is worth proportionally more to a late arrival (+25%) than to an anchor holder (+8%). That asymmetry is deliberate.

worked_example: Two wallets each hold a minimum of 1,000,000 tokens across every checkpoint. Wallet A held at the anchor slot: weight 3,000,000. Wallet B bought after the announcement and first appears at the final checkpoint: weight 1,000,000. A receives three times what B receives. If B also finds the entropy, B's weight becomes 1,250,000 and the gap narrows to 2.4x.
commitmentAlgo: SHA-256 of: checkpoint unix timestamps joined by ',', then '|', then a 16-byte hex nonce
commitmentCovers: The checkpoint TIMINGS and the nonce. It does not cover the payout formula, which is versioned in this file and amended in public.

seasonTwo.statusNote: The RULE is committed now. The amount and the date are not promised and are explicitly at the source wallet's discretion. This is published in advance for one reason: so that nobody can claim afterwards that the retention rule was invented once it was convenient.
seasonTwo.rule: Season two weight = (minimum balance across the season-two checkpoints) x (tenure multiplier, carried over) x (retention multiplier). The retention multiplier is measured on how much of your SEASON ONE allocation you still hold when season two is measured.
seasonTwo.why: Airdrops normally get sold within the hour, because a token you were given for free has no anchor. Publishing the retention rule before season one lands changes what the tokens are: holding them becomes the qualification for the larger pool rather than a sentimental choice. It produces the behaviour a vesting contract produces, without a vesting contract, a cliff, or any code that could be exploited. Nobody is locked. Everyone is simply told, in advance and in public, what selling costs them.
seasonTwo.recursion: Retention is measured with the same instrument as everything else on this page — the minimum balance across undisclosed checkpoints. Your season one tokens are not tracked separately or tagged in any way; they are simply part of the floor you are measured on. Sell them and your floor drops. The rule does not need to know which tokens were which.
seasonTwo.disclaimer: No allocation is owed to anyone in either season. Season two may be smaller than the ceiling, later than anyone expects, or may not happen. What is committed here is the rule that would govern it, not its existence.

amendments.change: Added the window close (2026-08-18T15:49:18Z) as a mandatory measurement counting toward the minimum-balance base, alongside the anchor and the five checkpoints. Its time is public. Nothing else changed.
amendments.reason: The five committed checkpoint times cluster in the first nine days of the fourteen-day window, with the last landing on 13 August. That left 5.44 days at the end during which a sale would never have been measured - an unintended free exit. Random draws clump; this one clumped. Rather than move the committed times, the gap is closed by adding a measurement at the close, whose time is public and therefore cannot be gamed.
amendments.note: The commitment hash 9a874b24e0c28700add51a7726e5d508b8230238423172015845ea019a2419d0 covers the five checkpoint timings and the nonce. It is untouched and still verifies against the original preimage. The close measurement is deliberately NOT part of the hash - it does not need to be secret, because its time was already published when the window was announced. Amended before any checkpoint had passed: the window opened at 15:49:18Z and the first checkpoint is not until 6 August.
amendments.sideEffect: One consequence worth stating plainly: because the base is a minimum across the anchor, all five checkpoints AND the close, a wallet that buys after the final checkpoint has a balance of zero at earlier checkpoints and therefore a weight of zero. Buying late enough is worth nothing at all. Since the checkpoint times are secret, there is no way to know when that cutoff has passed.

amendments.change: Replaced the hard retroactive gate with a tenure multiplier, and published the pool cap. Version 1 paid only wallets present at the anchor slot, which meant a buyer arriving after the announcement had a weight of exactly zero. Version 2 lets any holder qualify, pays anchor holders 3x, and scales down to 1x for the latest arrivals. The minimum-balance base is unchanged.
amendments.reason: Version 1 was unfarmable and therefore inert: it rewarded people who had already bought and gave nobody a reason to buy. The anti-dump property was the good part and it survives intact — you are still paid on your floor, so claiming and selling still caps you at the trough. What changed is that arriving late is now worth something instead of nothing.
amendments.note: The commitment hash covers the checkpoint timings and the nonce only. It is unchanged and remains valid against the original preimage. No distribution had occurred, and no checkpoint had been taken, at the time of this amendment. The diff is in the public git history of this file.
